parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A child stands on a scooter on horizontal ground. The combined mass of the child and the scooter is $16\text{ kg}$.
The child starts from rest and pushes once on the ground with her foot which causes her to accelerate. The push lasts for a time of $1.1\text{ s}$. The speed of the child and the scooter after the push is $0.60\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Determine the average resultant force acting horizontally on the child and the scooter during the push.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Later, the child in (b) travels down a slope at a constant angle to the horizontal, as shown in Fig. 2.1.
{{figure:figure_2_1}}
Fig. 2.1 (not to scale)
At point A her speed is $0.60\text{ m s}^{-1}$. She has a constant acceleration of $0.85\text{ m s}^{-2}$ parallel to the slope. After a time of $3.7\text{ s}$, she reaches point B.
Calculate the distance $x$ travelled by the child along the slope from A to B.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.part_stem:
At point B, the child in (c) applies the brake with a constant force to maintain a constant velocity. Point C is $18\text{ m}$ from point B, as shown in Fig. 2.2.
{{figure:figure_2_2}}
Fig. 2.2 (not to scale)
The work done by the braking force between B and C is $250\text{ J}$.
parts.text: Determine the magnitude of the braking force.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
On Fig. 2.3, sketch the variation of the kinetic energy of the child and scooter with distance travelled from point A to point C.
Numerical values for kinetic energy are not required.
